claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for your help. I have one child I'd like to check eligibility for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know! That's helpful context.

**What is your child's name?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Now I have a few questions to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's useful information.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that information.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have a right to reside here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**What is your nationality, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex your biological child, adopted child, or are you his legal guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's my son, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Does Alex live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex currently working or earning any income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time at the supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I believe I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the criteria:

According to Child Benefit rules, a child must generally be under 16 years old to qualify. However, there are some exceptions for children aged 16-19 who are in full-time education or approved training.

Since Alex is 17 years old and not in full-time education or training, but is instead working full-time, he would not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**
- Child Benefit is generally available for children under 16 years old
- There is an exception for 16-19 year olds who are in full-time education or approved training
- Alex is 17 and working full-time, rather than being in education or training, so he does not qualify

If Alex were to return to full-time education or an approved training course, his eligibility status could change. Is there anything else I can help you with?
